I need to send a quarterly update to our investors. I'm the founder of a scheduling app for physical therapy clinics. We have 6 people.

Numbers for the quarter:
- Monthly recurring revenue is $41,000, the same as three months ago.
- We added 9 clinics and lost 4. One of the 4 was our largest customer, a 12-clinic chain that paid $5,500 a month. They moved to the scheduler built into their electronic records system.
- We have $480,000 in the bank and lose about $44,000 a month.
- Clinics that use our automatic text reminders have a no-show rate of 7%, against 13% before they started.
- I didn't send updates for the last two quarters.
- Next month we start selling the reminder feature on its own for $150 a month.

Under 500 words. It goes to 11 investors.

Before I draft, a few questions. Your answers would change what the update says:

1. **What's the plan for the runway?** $480k at $44k a month is about 11 months. Are you raising, cutting costs, or aiming to break even? If you have a target date or MRR number, include it.
2. **What do you want from these 11 investors?** For example, intros to PT chains, intros to electronic records vendors, advice on pricing, or bridge money. Or is this update only to inform them?
3. **Do you have early evidence for the $150 reminder product?** That could be a waitlist, pilot clinics, letters of intent, or conversations with clinics whose records system already has a scheduler. Also, who is the main buyer: new clinics, or clinics like the chain you lost?
4. **Are other customers likely to leave the same way?** Are any other customers on records systems that have a built-in scheduler? And roughly how many clinics are behind the 13% → 7% no-show figure?
5. **Why did the last two updates not go out?** One honest sentence is enough. Or tell me if you'd rather just acknowledge the gap and commit to a schedule.

If you don't know something, say so and I'll write the update without it.

1. I don't have a set plan for the runway yet. Leave it out.
2. 20 minutes on the phone with each of them, and introductions to clinic chains.
3. 6 clinics have said they'll buy the reminder feature on its own when it launches December 1. I don't know yet who the main buyer will be.
4. Yes. Two other customers use the same records system as the chain that left. Together they pay $3,800 a month. I can't promise they won't leave the same way. I don't know offhand how many clinics are behind the no-show numbers.
5. The numbers were flat and I didn't want to send bad news. That's the only reason. Going forward I can commit to an update in the first week of every quarter, with the next one on January 7. I can also send a monthly one-page set of numbers to any investor who asks for it.

I computed the "about 11 months" figure from $480,000 ÷ $44,000. I didn't add a runway plan, as you asked. The no-show figures don't give a number of clinics because you didn't have it. If you can add it before sending, it will make that result more convincing. Fill in the subject's quarter label and your name. The update is about 430 words.

Subject: Quarterly update: flat quarter, a big customer loss, and a new product launching Dec 1

Hi all,

First, an apology. This is your first update in six months. The numbers were flat and I didn't want to send bad news. That was the wrong call, because you should hear bad news as soon as I have it. From now on you'll get an update in the first week of every quarter, with the next one on January 7. I'll also send a one-page set of numbers every month to anyone who wants it. Just reply and ask.

**The numbers**
- Monthly recurring revenue: $41,000, the same as three months ago
- Clinics: 9 added, 4 lost
- Cash: $480,000 in the bank. We lose about $44,000 a month, which leaves about 11 months at the current rate.
- Team: 6 people

**What happened**
Revenue is flat because the new clinics only made up for the ones we lost. The biggest loss was our largest customer, a 12-clinic chain paying $5,500 a month. They moved to the scheduler built into their electronic records system. That is the main risk to our business. When a clinic's records system has a scheduler that's good enough, we're competing with something they already pay for.

This may not be the last such loss. Two other customers use the same records system, and together they pay $3,800 a month. I can't promise they'll stay.

**What's working**
Clinics that use our automatic text reminders have a no-show rate of 7%, down from 13% before they started. A no-show is an appointment slot the clinic can't bill for. Reminders are where we show the clearest results.

**What's next**
On December 1 we start selling the reminder feature on its own for $150 a month. A clinic can buy it without replacing its scheduler. Six clinics have already said they'll buy it at launch. I don't know yet who the main buyer will be: new clinics, or clinics like the chain we lost. The January update will report what we learn.

**Two asks**
1. **A 20-minute phone call with each of you.** I'd like to walk you through the reminder launch and the risk from records-system schedulers, and hear what you think. Please reply with a few times that work for you.
2. **Introductions to clinic chains.** If you know someone who owns or runs a physical therapy chain, an introduction would help a great deal.

I know this isn't the update any of us wanted. You'll hear from me on January 7, whatever the numbers say.

Thanks,
[Your name]
